newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala seeks regional approach to free trade.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala seeks regional approach to free trade.

text.p: Central America should negotiate any free trade treaties as a bloc, the Guatemalan Economy Minister said on Wednesday.

Juan Mauricio Wurmser told reporters a Central American council of ministers responsible for economic integration will meet in Nicaragua on Thursday to talk about free trade issues and to establish a priority for negotiations with different countries outside the region.

Wurmser said while Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador are deep in free trade talks with Mexico, other countries, including Panama, Chile and the Caribbean basin have expressed interest in free trade talks with Central America.
"Guatemala's position is that the Central American region must, above all, try to maintain a policy of joint negotiation," Wurmser said.
Because of limited negotiating capacity, it is important for Central America to complete the free trade negotiations with Mexico before entering other important talks, the minister said.
Wurmser said the next round of talks between the so-called Northern Triangle of Central American nations and Mexico would take place in Mexico the second week of February.
